Creator Rod Serling adhered (largely) to a set of rules for each episode, in which ordinary characters find themselves in extraordinary settings, with one miracle or imaginative circumstance, and the premise is established quickly to keep the story tight and engaging. title: ‘The redistricting arms race is not going to come to an end any time soon,’ expert says as several states consider redrawing their congressional maps before the 2028 presidential election
content:
At least four states are considering redrawing their congressional maps before the 2028 presidential election, raising the prospect of another partisan battle over control of the House. The mid-decade redistricting arms race reshaped the 2026 midterms, but the results did not consistently benefit the parties that pursued new maps. With Maryland, Mississippi, New York and Wisconsin weighing further changes ahead of 2028, an expert says the redistricting arms race is unlikely to “end any time soon.”

Mid-decade redistricting produced mixed results in 2026

Congressional boundaries are generally redrawn after each decennial census, although courts can require changes when maps violate the law. Before the 2026 midterms, however, states increasingly pursued redistricting for partisan advantage. The redistricting effort began in Texas, where Republicans, with President Donald Trump‘s support, sought to protect their House majority. However, the party gained only one redrawn seat near Dallas, while Democrats flipped two Republican-held districts in South Texas. California, Alabama, Florida, North Carolina and Tennessee also redrew their maps. Ohio and Utah followed court orders, while efforts in Indiana, Missouri and Virginia failed.

The Supreme Court’s Louisiana v. Callais ruling further complicated the process. The decision found that Louisiana’s map containing two majority-Black districts constituted a racial gerrymander and was seen as weakening the Voting Rights Act. Other states subsequently used the ruling to eliminate majority-Black, Democratic-leaning seats.

Maryland and Mississippi consider new maps

Maryland voters approved a constitutional amendment that could allow Democrats to redraw the state’s congressional boundaries before 2028.

According to reports, the potential target is Republican Rep. Andy Harris’s 1st District, which covers much of the conservative Eastern Shore. An earlier attempt was blocked by a judge in 2022, and Democratic Senate President Bill Ferguson had declined to pursue another redraw. University at Buffalo political science professor Shawn Donahue described Maryland as the state “most likely” to redistrict. “It’s a heavily democratic state, so it wouldn’t take a whole lot of moving around people to kind of eliminate that member,” he said.

Mississippi Gov. Tate Reeves has also expressed interest in changing the map to make Democratic Rep. Bennie Thompson’s district more conservative. In May, Reeves declared, “It is not a question of if, it’s a question of when.” However, strong Democratic performances in the midterms have raised questions about whether Republicans will pursue the plan.

New York and Wisconsin explore redistricting options

New York Democrats have advanced a constitutional amendment allowing mid-decade redistricting, although it must be first approved by voters. Potential targets include Republican-held districts on Long Island, Staten Island and upstate New York. Gov. Kathy Hochul previously called redistricting a “right for our democracy.”

In Wisconsin, Democratic Governor-elect David Crowley has promised to sign a redistricting bill if it reaches his desk. Changes could affect Democratic Representatives-elect Mitchell Berman and Rebecca Cooke, whose districts Trump carried in 2024.

‘The redistricting arms race is not going to come to an end any time soon,’ expert says

Donahue said on Monday that “the redistricting arms race is not going to come to an end any time soon.” He also said the prospect of redistricting had increased Black voter participation in Mississippi and South Carolina. “Even the threat of mid-decade redistricting supercharged the Black vote share in both of those states,” he said. “I think that if you’re Democrats right now, you think you have the chance to do some stuff on your side. And if you’re Republicans, you’re probably looking down the barrel at the next round of redistricting in 2032…That seats are gonna move south. Maybe they think it’s maybe still in their best interests,” Donahue added.

title: US citizen shot by ICE officer during California immigration operation files lawsuit against Trump admin seeking more than $25 million in damages
content:
A U.S. citizen shot by an ICE officer during an immigration operation in Southern California has filed a lawsuit seeking more than $25 million in damages from the Trump administration. Carlos Jimenez filed a complaint on November 6, accusing federal agents of using excessive force, fabricating evidence and denying him adequate medical treatment after the shooting. The lawsuit followed the dismissal of federal charges against him and disputes the government’s account of what happened.

Carlos Jimenez alleges an ICE officer shot him during an attempted U-turn

The 54-page complaint alleges that Jimenez approached federal immigration agents to warn them that children would soon gather at a nearby school bus stop. After ICE officer Eusebio Ortiz allegedly threatened to shoot him if he did not leave, Jimenez attempted to turn his Lexus around. According to the lawsuit, Ortiz fired several rounds through the vehicle’s rear passenger-side window, striking Jimenez in the back and shoulder. He suffered a displaced fracture of his right shoulder blade, with bullet fragments remaining near his right lung.

The complaint also alleged that FBI agents removed Jimenez from his hospital bed, “handcuffed him with a leather waist restraint” and questioned him while he was still seriously injured. It says he “kept bleeding and vomiting in the agents’ van” and was told not to “ruin their vehicle.”

Federal prosecutors initially charged Carlos Jimenez

Federal prosecutors subsequently charged Jimenez with assaulting an officer with his vehicle, and a grand jury indicted him on November 18, 2025. The Department of Homeland Security (DHS) maintained that Jimenez had not been the target of the operation and was ordered to leave before reversing toward officers, prompting Ortiz to fire “defensive shots.” However, Jimenez’s lawyer disputed that account, arguing that he was performing a three-point turn and had already begun moving forward when he was shot.

The case later became the subject of a dispute over evidence. Jimenez’s complaint accused FBI Special Agent Estevan R. Banuelos of fabricating statements attributed to witnesses Manuel Villareal and Beatrice Morales. An FBI report suggested Jimenez had enough room to drive forward, but the witnesses reportedly told a defense investigator that they had not provided such an estimate and had not witnessed the shooting.

Judge orders government disclosure before dismissing criminal case against Carlos Jimenez

In early May, U.S. District Judge Kenly Kiya Kato ordered the government to disclose relevant communications, including those stored on agents’ personal and government-issued phones. Jimenez subsequently entered a diversion agreement and completed its conditions. On November 2, Kato dismissed the indictment with prejudice, meaning the charge cannot be refiled, bringing the criminal prosecution to an end. It is worth noting that the dismissal did not establish that the officers had acted unlawfully.

The Justice Department said Jimenez had requested diversion and that prosecutors sought dismissal after he completed the agreement. A spokesperson noted that he had no criminal history and said the arrangement had spared him “serious, lifelong consequences.” The spokesperson also maintained that a grand jury had found probable cause to indict him.

Lawsuit seeks more than $25 million in damages

Jimenez’s lawsuit names Ortiz, two Customs and Border Protection officers identified as N. Jimenez and S. Cosey, FBI Special Agent Banuelos, San Bernardino County and the Trump administration, along with 20 unnamed defendants. It brings 13 claims, including excessive force, false arrest, malicious prosecution and denial of medical care. Jimenez is seeking $25 million in non-economic damages, along with nearly $179,000 for medical expenses, lost wages, property damage and other losses.

The case came amid broader scrutiny of the use of aggressive force by federal immigration enforcement. According to The Trace’s tracker, at least 32 shootings involving federal immigration agents have been reported since President Donald Trump took office and enforced his mass deportation agenda, resulting in at least nine deaths and 15 injuries.

title: Former senior White House adviser Calley Means says ‘there is a very concentrated group of people in the Trump administration’ who are ‘antagonistic to what people voted for’
content:
Former senior White House and Health and Human Services (HHS) adviser Calley Means has accused former White House chief of staff Susie Wiles and other Trump administration officials of putting lobbying interests ahead of President Donald Trump’s health agenda.

Speaking on The Joe Rogan Experience and later to CBS News, Means alleged that aides pushed for a pathway to approve fruit-flavored vapes while resisting efforts to improve children’s diets. Notably, Means’ accusations have been denied by Wiles, other officials and lobbyist Brian Ballard, exposing growing tensions within the administration.

Calley Means accuses Trump aides of catering to lobbyists

Explaining why he left the administration, Means told Rogan on the podcast, “The simple reality in why I left is that there is a very concentrated group of people in the Trump administration that are antagonistic to what people voted for.”

He alleged that Wiles and other aides pressured HHS and the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) to create a pathway for fruit-flavored vapes following lobbying by tobacco interests connected to Ballard Partners. Means also claimed Wiles repeatedly invoked the need to raise money for the midterms, telling him, “We need money for the midterms, Calley. We need money for the midterms.”

In an interview with CBS News’ Face the Nation, Means broadened his accusations beyond vaping. “Underneath Trump’s nose, in many cases, you had a group of former lobbyists, catering to the vaping industry, catering to the ultra-processed food industry, catering to the pharmaceutical industry, catering to the pesticide industry and doing their bidding with an excuse that we need their money for the midterms and really need to actually go against what voters said,” he said.

Calley Means responds to possibility of legal action

Means’ allegations have focused particularly on flavored vapes and glyphosate, a pesticide-related issue. On Sunday, November 8, he publicly requested that records concerning Wiles’ influence on health policy be preserved, citing the possibility of legal action over his interviews.

“In light of suggestions that Susie Wiles and James Blair may pursue legal action over my Joe Rogan interview, I am publicly requesting that she, Ballard Partners, Continental Strategy, and other relevant parties immediately preserve all potentially relevant records and communications,” he wrote on X.

Susie Wiles and Ballard Partners reject allegations

James Blair, a former deputy to Wiles, denied promoting flavored vaping. “I didn’t promote flavored vaping specifically at all,” he told CBS News, accusing Means of “intentionally misrepresenting my role and my responsibility because he opposes the issue entirely.”

Wiles also denied Means’ account of her arranging a meeting between tobacco representatives and Trump at his golf course. Ballard rejected claims that his firm communicated with Wiles or the White House about fruit-flavored vapes or glyphosate. He said its work on vaping had focused on “illegal, unregulated vapes.”

MAHA had ‘found a champion in President Trump’

Means’ accusations came amid broader disagreements between MAHA-aligned lawmakers and supporters and the Trump administration over pesticide regulation, food policy and the surgeon general nomination.

In a statement to Newsweek, White House spokesperson Allison Schuster said MAHA had “found a champion in President Trump,” adding, “The Administration has already secured extensive victories for the MAHA Agenda, including overhauling the dietary guidelines for Americans, axing artificial ingredients in our food supply, and investing in regenerative farming. President Trump and Secretary Kennedy continue to work around the clock to deliver more wins for the American people.”

title: Pete Hegseth’s entourage scolded by sentinel for laughing during visit to the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier: ‘All visitors will maintain an atmosphere of silence and respect at all times’
content:
Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth‘s entourage was reprimanded by a military sentinel at the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier after laughter erupted during a Veterans Day visit to Arlington National Cemetery.

The viral confrontation

The incident unfolded on Wednesday, November 11, as Hegseth and several members of his inner circle visited the solemn memorial, prompting the guard on duty to interrupt his patrol and demand silence.

Viral footage of the confrontation showed Hegseth’s entourage, dressed in dark suits, ascending the marble steps of the Memorial Amphitheater near the tomb.

The sentinel, wearing ceremonial dress blues and carrying a rifle, stopped marching after laughter could be heard coming from the group.

“All visitors will maintain an atmosphere of silence and respect at all times,” the sentinel shouted, turning toward the group as it departed the memorial.

Pete Hegseth’s Memorial Day visit

Hegseth had been posing for photographs alongside his wife, Jennifer, and several senior Pentagon officials, including chief of staff Ricky Buria, deputy chief of staff Patrick Weaver and senior adviser Tami Radabaugh.

However, the footage did not establish who was laughing or whether Hegseth himself participated.

The Pentagon acknowledged the incident, defending the secretary’s commitment to honoring military service members while recognizing the sentinel’s intervention.

In a recent statement, Pentagon spokesman Sean Parnell said, “The Secretary and the entire Department have always honored — and will always honor — the sacrifices our military men and women have made to keep America safe. While commemorating this solemn day, a soldier correctly and respectfully reminded everyone to maintain decorum.”

Political pressure on Pete Hegseth

The confrontation occurred amid mounting political pressure on Hegseth, whose Pentagon leadership has faced scrutiny over military operations involving Iran and Venezuela, alongside allegations concerning civilian treatment and suspected drug-trafficking vessels.

Just one day earlier, the House voted to refer eight articles of impeachment against Hegseth to the Judiciary Committee, effectively stalling efforts to remove him from office.

Hegseth has dismissed the allegations as politically motivated, while President Donald Trump has repeatedly defended his defense secretary, including during the Veterans Day Arlington ceremony.

The Tomb of the Unknown Soldier

The Tomb of the Unknown Soldier is among America’s most solemn military memorials, honoring unidentified service members who died defending the nation.

The memorial has been guarded continuously since July 2, 1937, with the Army’s 3rd U.S. Infantry Regiment, known as “The Old Guard,” assuming responsibility in 1948.

Sentinels follow a precise ceremonial routine, marching 21 steps along a 63-foot mat before pausing for 21 seconds while facing the tomb.

Guards undergo extensive training and five phases of testing before earning the prestigious Tomb Guard Identification Badge.

Visitors are expected to remain silent and show respect throughout the ceremony, regardless of rank or position.

title: Scott Bessent moves to a military base after getting death threats from Iran, spokesperson says President Donald Trump’s treasury secretary ‘will not be deterred by the Iranian regime’s threats’
content:
Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has moved out of his Washington-area home and onto a military base following threats against his life from Iran, according to people familiar with the matter. U.S. officials reportedly determined that Iranian plots targeting current and former American officials had become more advanced, with intelligence identifying Bessent as a potential target.

Scott Bessent relocates after intelligence identifies Iranian threats

Three people familiar with the matter said Bessent recently moved to a military base after U.S. officials assessed threats against him as “serious.” The intelligence review also indicated that Iranian plotting against American officials had reached a more advanced stage in recent weeks, although the precise severity of the threats remains unclear. U.S. officials have said that although Iran has limited capacity to carry out large-scale attacks in the U.S. and overseas, its ability to carry out specific threats against individuals is serious.

Bessent has led an economic pressure campaign against Tehran since August, using tougher sanctions and restrictions on trade routes to isolate Iran financially. People familiar with the intelligence said that role has made him one of the Trump administration officials Iran most wants to harm. A Treasury Department spokesperson said Bessent remains committed to the campaign and “will not be deterred by the Iranian regime’s threats.”

Economic pressure campaign aims to weaken Tehran

A central objective of Bessent’s campaign is to cut off funding to the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC), Iran’s most powerful military institution, which also controls much of the country’s economy. The Trump administration hopes financial pressure will reduce the need to resume major military operations in the Iran war, a deeply unpopular conflict President Donald Trump has repeatedly promised to end.

Bessent and other officials say sanctions are shrinking Iran’s economy, weakening its currency and worsening living standards. However, U.S. intelligence indicates that Iran’s hard-line leadership remains determined to retain power despite the economic damage.

Senior Trump administration officials moved into protected housing

Bessent is the latest senior administration official to leave a Washington-area residence for military or other protected housing. At least half a dozen officials relocated last year, including Stephen Miller, now the White House chief of staff, and then-Attorney General Pam Bondi.

The Trump administration has not disclosed the full scope of threats against its senior officials, which do not all involve Iran. For instance, Bondi’s security concerns reportedly increased after the U.S. military captured former Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro in Caracas and brought him to New York to face federal criminal charges.

Iran threats prompt security measures

Last month, the U.S. government placed employees across the Middle East on heightened alert and reduced staffing at several embassies and consulates. The security measures followed intelligence indicating that Iran was in advanced stages of planning attacks against Americans. The U.S. military also abruptly relocated bombers from a base in the United Kingdom following a suspected terrorist plot against the facility.

According to reports, Iran has been targeting Trump since January 2020, when he ordered a drone strike that killed Major General Qassim Suleimani, commander of the IRGC’s Quds Force. In 2024, federal prosecutors charged Farhad Shakeri, whom they described as a Revolutionary Guard operative, with plotting to assassinate Trump in retaliation for Suleimani’s death.

Several national security officials involved in the planning of the 2020 Suleimani strike also faced Iranian threats. The Biden administration maintained security details for some of them, but Trump revoked protections almost immediately after returning to office.

title: Suspected Iran-backed operative allegedly coordinated terror plot targeting US troops in Britain from behind bars in Brooklyn
content:
A suspected Iran-backed operative allegedly coordinated a terrorist plot targeting U.S. troops at Britain’s RAF Fairford air base while being detained at a federal jail in Brooklyn, according to a newly unsealed indictment. Mohammad Baqer Saad Dawood al-Saadi is accused of using coded messages and phone calls with relatives in Iraq to communicate with two alleged co-conspirators. According to reports, the charges form part of a wider investigation into nearly 20 suspected attacks against Jewish communities and military targets in Europe and the U.S.

Mohammad Baqer Saad Dawood al-Saadi allegedly coordinated RAF Fairford plot from jail

The superseding indictment, unsealed on Tuesday, November 10, alleges that al-Saadi used calls with family members in Iraq to pass coded messages to co-defendants Mohsen Mohajeri and Mohammad Ali al-Hassani ahead of a suspected September plot targeting RAF Fairford. The alleged operation came to light after five men were detained shortly after midnight on September 27, following reports of three suspicious vans traveling toward the British military base. A sixth suspect, a British-Iranian dual national, was arrested several days later. However, all six were subsequently released by British authorities on bail.

U.K. Prime Minister Andy Burnham said in October that the suspected plot was “highly likely” to have been coordinated in Iran and “almost certainly” directed by the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC), although the embattled nation has denied involvement. The U.S. subsequently withdrew bombers stationed at RAF Fairford, redeploying them to their home bases.

Three defendants accused of plotting nearly 20 attacks

The unsealed indictment names three defendants: al-Saadi, who’s a dual Iranian-Iraqi national, Mohajeri, who’s an Iranian national and al-Hassani, who’s an Iraqi national. Only al-Saadi, who was 32 when arrested, is currently in U.S. custody. In June, al-Saadi pleaded not guilty to charges alleging he plotted at least 18 attacks across Europe in retaliation for the U.S. and Israel’s war with Iran. He described himself as a “prisoner of war.” Prosecutors identified him as a commander of Kata’ib Hezbollah, which, alongside the IRGC, is designated a foreign terrorist organization by the United States.

FBI Director Kash Patel said the indictment “shows the determination of Iran to commit terrorist attacks in Europe and the U.S.”

U.S. Attorney Jamie McDonald said, “The threat presented by Iran and Iran-backed terrorist groups to America and our allies is not hypothetical — it is very real.”

Attorney General Todd Blanche added, “Anyone who plans a terrorist plot on a military base housing American service members will be prosecuted by the United States government.”

Prosecutors detail alleged plans targeting Jewish institutions

Prosecutors say al-Saadi’s alleged activities date back nearly a decade, accusing him of having “conspired and urged others to commit violent attacks” against the U.S. and American citizens on behalf of Iran-linked terrorist organizations.

In March and April, he allegedly attempted to organize attacks against Jewish institutions, including a New York City synagogue. A May criminal complaint alleged he sent an undercover officer photographs and maps of a prominent Manhattan synagogue and two institutions in Los Angeles and Scottsdale, Arizona, directing the officer to attack them. They also discussed whether to use an improvised explosive device or “set the place on fire.” None of the attacks ultimately occurred.

Defense contests claims of coded communications

Al-Saadi’s attorneys challenged prosecutors’ interpretation of his jail calls, arguing that references to coded language are speculative. An October 13 filing stated that the government provided no FBI declaration establishing that al-Saadi or his relatives had used coded messages. “It provides only the government’s lawyers’ speculation about conversations that were translated from Arabic,” the attorneys wrote, arguing that the calls did not justify his extreme isolation.

The defense also contested the interpretation of a call in which al-Saadi’s sister mentioned his growing visibility on TikTok. Prosecutors said he directed relatives to contact Mohajeri, allegedly using the alias Sayyid Abbas, about media coverage. His lawyers argued that his comments amount to protected advocacy about his case.

title: Prince William and Kate Middleton Celebrate King Charles’ 78th Birthday
content:
King Charles III kicked off his 78th birthday with a special tribute from his son Prince William and wife Princess Kate Middleton — with a subtle assist from Sir Elton John.

“With a very happy birthday to His Majesty The King,” William and Kate, both 44, wrote via Instagram Stories on Saturday, November 14.

The Prince and Princess of Wales also reposted the official Royal Family account’s birthday message.

“Happy Birthday to His Majesty The King! 🎊🎂,” a caption read, alongside a photo of Charles posing with the “Rocket Man” singer, 79. “Tune in to a special edition of @EltonJohn’s Rocket Hour to celebrate 50 years of @KingsTrust, from 9am GMT today on @AppleMusic.”

King Charles' Relationship With Daughter-in-Law Kate Through the Years 

John responded in the comments section, writing, “Happy Birthday to His Majesty!”

The accomplished singer and Charles secretly filmed an episode of John’s radio show at Apple Music’s recording studio in October.

“Hi, I’m Elton John and welcome to my ‘Rocket Hour,’” he began in a teaser clip for the podcast episode. “This week, I have a special guest, and I really mean a special guest. I’m so excited to hear what he’s going to say about music, about the King’s Trust [his eponymous nonprofit] and memories that we both share.”

John, who was knighted in 1998 by the regent’s late mother Queen Elizabeth II, has a long history with Charles and the royal family.

“You’ve informed me of things that I didn’t know, and it’s reaffirmed in my mind what a great and wonderful thing you set up with the Prince’s Trust years ago and continue to do on a daily basis these days,” John told the monarch during the episode. “Championing young people is something I know you’ve always loved to do in your life anyway, but for the arts and music, it’s really important.”

John added, “The fact that you’ve done this and you continue to do it is an incredible feather in your cap, and I congratulate you.”

Charles was grateful for John’s kind words.

Prince William Addresses King Charles III's Cancer Diagnosis

“We are so richly blessed with the talents of our musicians, singers and performers, particularly yourself, if I may say so,” Charles noted. “You’ve become such a national treasure after all these years of everything you’ve done for so many people.”

After John subsequently joked he would appear on Antiques Roadshow next in an apparent self-aware quip about his age, Charles added with a laugh, “Well, anyway, join the club.”

Sharing a clip to Facebook, John opened up about welcoming the king to his eponymous show.

“It was a great privilege to welcome The King to my Rocket Hour show, marking the 50th anniversary of The King’s Trust which has transformed the lives of countless young people,” a caption read.

title: Joe Jonas and Girlfriend Tatiana Gabriela Split After 1 Year of Dating
content:
It’s over. Joe Jonas and model Tatiana Gabriela have broken up after dating for just over one year.

“They had a really fun summer traveling together, but then things shifted in the relationship,” a source with knowledge can exclusively confirm to Us. “Things started to shift as Joe got busier with work commitments and they were spending more time apart.”

The insider continued, “They had a lot of fun together and were a really good match, so friends are still hopeful they might be able to work things out. But right now, they just have different lifestyles.”

Joe, 37, and his brothers, Nick Jonas and Kevin Jonas, are booked through the end of the year with their Burning Up Tour All Over Again, which is scheduled to wrap up with two pre-Christmas shows in Newark on December 21 and December 22. He also coparents daughters Willa, 6, and Delphine, 4, with his ex-wife Sophie Turner, who lives in London.

Joe Jonas' Dating History Through the Years

“Joe has a lot on his plate between work and being a dad, and that can be a lot for someone to take on,” the source shared with Us.

Us has reached out to representatives for both stars for comment.

Fans initially speculated that Joe and Gabriela may have gone their separate ways after she reposted a TikTok video that said, “Thought I saw love in your eyes but it was just a reflection of mine.”

Nearly one year earlier, Joe first hinted at his connection to Gabriela in January by “liking” one of her Instagram posts and commenting with a “drooling” emoji.

A source exclusively confirmed to Us that same month that Joe had recently introduced Gabriela as his girlfriend to his friends and family, his two children and ex Turner. (He and the Game of Thrones actress, 30, finalized their divorce in September 2024.)

“[Joe and Gabriela] started seeing each other at the end of the summer [in 2025],” the insider revealed at the time.

The couple finally hard-launched their relationship in April with an Instagram carousel, including a black-and-white photo of Gabriela resting her arms around the Jonas Brothers star’s neck. The musician also shared a vlog from a recent trip to Puerto Rico, showing Gabriela trying to teach Joe how to speak Spanish and enjoying lots of the local cuisine.

“She’s helping with my Spanish,” Joe declared in the YouTube video, adding, “Then we went to a waterfall, we jumped in, it was so nice.”

Prior to his year-long relationship with Gabriela, Joe had a brief romance with model Stormi Bree in 2024.

“I was seeing somebody at the time, and I was kind of having this idea of dating again. It was really scary and intimidating,” Joe confirmed during a TalkShopLive livestream in May 2025. “Love takes different shapes and forms, and I was rediscovering what that was.”

A source told Us in May 2024 that Joe and Bree, 35, had hit pause on seeing each other because of the demands of their busy schedules.

“Joe has a very busy schedule between his kids and his career, so his romantic life has to take a back seat for now,” the insider explained.

Sophie Turner Recalls Marriage to Joe Jonas: 'A Beautiful Relationship'

Joe was previously married to Turner for four years before they announced their separation in September 2023.

“After four wonderful years of marriage we have mutually decided to amicably end our marriage,” Joe and Turner said in a joint statement at the time. “There are many speculative narratives as to why, but truly this is a united decision, and we sincerely hope that everyone can respect our wishes for privacy for us and our children.”

The exes ultimately finalized their divorce settlement in September 2024 after a full year of negotiations.

“Afer a productive and successful mediation, we have agreed that the children will spend time equally in loving homes in both the U.S. and the U.K.,” they told Us in a statement at the time. “We look forward to being great coparents.”

title: Shane Gillis Breaks Silence on Controversial 'SNL' Monologue Shaming Women
content:
Shane Gillis is addressing his controversial Saturday Night Live monologue in which the comedian shamed women for their workout attire.

“Not to defend SNL — they don’t approve it,” Gillis, 38, said while appearing on the Friday, November 13, episode of “The Joe Rogan Experience” podcast, revealing that SNL personnel did not pre-approve his remarks during the October 10 show. “I mean, they could shut it down.”

He then recalled what he said he told the show before he took the live stage.

“I’m giving you a solid C minus of a monologue, but I promise there’s no controversy,” Gillis said.

'Saturday Night Live UK' Calls Shane Gillis a 'C***' in Swipe at 'SNL' US

In October, Gillis came under fire after calling women who go to the gym to workout “whores” for how they dress.

“I haven’t been to the gym in so long, I didn’t know women just dress like whores now? Look, I’m sorry, there’s no other way to describe [it],” the comedian lamented at the time. “Have you seen it? I’ve seen it. You’ve seen the shorts? They’re those neon, like, artificial bait-colored [shorts], and the wrinkles go around the cheeks and all combine at the butthole. And don’t look! You’re not allowed to look.”

Gillis’ remarks sparked instant backlash online, with many Hollywood stars speaking out in opposition of the comedian’s remarks in the wake of the Jane Doe Cornell gang rape allegations.

“Women wearing short shorts to the gym does not make them whores,” Dan Levy said in an Instagram video shared on October 11. “It makes the men calling them whores misogynists. There’s a difference there.”

The Schitt’s Creek alum added that he’s “seen more men’s nipples at the gym than I’ve ever seen women showing their bodies off.”

“But I’m speechless that something like that can exist on live national television,” he continued. “And to be perfectly honest, more men need to be standing up in opposition to it because it’s complacency that has created the environment [in] which women are sexually assaulted, and it’s a conversation as opposed to a crime.”

Lorne Michaels Calls Shane Gillis 'SNL' Casting Backlash an 'Overreaction'

He continued, “This is not a women’s issue. This is an everybody issue, because the more that men objectify women in the media, the more that other men see them as objects and treat them as objects. They are not objects. They are superior human beings to men, OK? And I’m sorry if this gets me in trouble with the internet, but f***.”

Others came to the comedian’s defense, including Dana Carvey, David Spade and Jimmy Carr, among others.

“I just didn’t understand the kerfuffle only because, to me, I just saw it as what we call it — I’ll just say it — a joke,” Carvey, 71, said during an October episode of the Fly the Wall podcast with Spade, 62. “Like, when you say jokes, you’re not literally saying women are whores. You are literally joking. Isn’t that kind of the idea? No? Did I just get canceled?”

During his Friday conversation with UFC commentator-turned-podcast host Joe Rogan, Gillis admitted that his joke was ill-received as a result of the “times.”

“[It] obviously had a lot to do with the climate,” he said. “The first time I got fired, I kept social media. This time, I just deleted everything immediately.” (Gillis was fired from SNL in 2019 after just four days among racist and homophobic comments from his podcast that had resurfaced online. SNL noted at the time that they were unaware of his “offensive” remarks. Gillis also released a statement but did not apologize for his comments.)

title: Protestors throw cartons of milk at Joe Biden, chant ‘blood on your hands’ at former president during surprise visit to Ireland
content:
Joe Biden faced a hostile reception during a surprise visit to Ireland on Tuesday, November 10, as pro-Palestinian protesters threw cartons of milk at the former president and chanted “blood on your hands” outside Trinity College Dublin. The former president, accompanied by wife Jill Biden, was attending a ceremony honoring their son, Hunter Biden. Three men were arrested following the confrontation, Irish police confirmed on Wednesday, November 11.

Protesters target Bidens as family leaves Trinity College

Videos circulating on social media showed demonstrators, some carrying Palestinian flags, throwing objects, including cartons of milk, toward the Bidens as they were escorted into a waiting car. Security personnel used an umbrella to shield the family, while protesters clashed with police. One man was seen being restrained on top of a car, and another pair of demonstrators were held back as a carton of milk burst open.

Harper Alderson, editor of Trinity’s University Times, told Irish broadcaster RTÉ that police had used pepper spray on two protesters. “The protest grew very large as the cars were moving through front square of the college,” she said. “Students were surrounding them and chanting ‘Genocide Joe’, ‘shame on you’ and ‘guards off our campus,’ among other things.”

Trinity College spokesperson Catherine O’Mahony said the protest escalated as the Bidens were leaving, prompting the arrival of Ireland’s police force, the Gardaí. “The Biden family left without incident. The protest dispersed soon after,” she said.

Three men arrested after the incident

Irish police said Wednesday that three adult men were arrested “in relation to a public order incident” at Trinity College Dublin. One man in his 50s was charged and is due to appear in court, while the other two were released without charge. 

The Bidens had attended the ceremony at the invitation of Trinity’s traditional Hist debating society, which dates back to 1770. Hunter received its Gold Medal for Outstanding Contribution to Public Discourse in recognition of his advocacy on American politics and media, as well as his work raising awareness of addiction and recovery. During his acceptance speech, Hunter discussed his struggles with addiction, family life and the experience of living in the public eye. “We are living in an age of bullies,” he said, adding that he had learned this from “my own scars.”

Gaza war remains a source of criticism against Joe Biden

The protest reflected longstanding Irish solidarity with the Palestinian cause. Flags, murals and graffiti supporting Palestine are common across the country, with many Irish people drawing parallels between the situation in Gaza and the occupied West Bank and Ireland’s own history of British colonial rule.

Joe has faced sustained criticism for continuing military aid and diplomatic support for Israel during the Gaza war, which began during his presidency, amid mounting civilian casualties and his administration’s failure to secure a ceasefire. The former president also repeatedly expressed concern over Palestinian suffering and civilian deaths and called for a two-state solution.

Bidens meet Irish prime minister amid former president’s health treatment

The Bidens, who have Irish ancestry, also met Taoiseach Micheál Martin. “We reflected on his strong Irish roots and previous visits, appreciating his lifelong support for Ireland,” the prime minister wrote on X.

The Ireland visit came days after the 83-year-old former president indicated he is scaling back public appearances promoting his upcoming memoir, Promise Me, America, as he undergoes treatment for an aggressive form of prostate cancer. “Some days are better than others,” he wrote on Sunday, November 8. “It hasn’t stopped me. But sometimes it slows me down,” Joe said, adding that his doctors are “encouraged by how I’ve responded to treatment.”

title: Tyriq Withers Quotes Meme in Daniel Kaluuya Interview During FAA Ground Stop
content:
Actors Tyriq Withers and Daniel Kaluuya found a way to laugh as their flight was one of thousands to be majorly delayed as a result of the Federal Aviation Administration’s (FAA) unprecedented nationwide ground stop.

“Today, we were headed back to Los Angeles. We got on the plane and we had to de-board, unfortunately,” Withers, 28, said during a Friday, November 13, interview with local Oregon news outlet KVAL 13 and after the FAA ordered all flights across the country grounded due to what was later described as “communication issues.”

“I just want to thank God for really protecting us, you know, post-blue wave as well,” the Reminders of Him actor continued.

Withers, referring to the Democratic Party’s overwhelming victory in the 2026 midterm elections, went on to parody a now-viral meme from a 2015 interview about the Bella Noche nightclub shooting. (A patron of the Louisiana establishment told WBRZ at the time that the incident had been upsetting because, “If you can’t go to Bella Noche, where the hell can you go?”)

Who Is Tyriq Withers? What to Know About the ‘Reminders of Him’ Star

He quipped, “I feel like it’s really upsetting me and my home girl ‘cause if you can’t go to the airport, where the hell can you go?”

Withers’ comments had Kaluyya, 27, in hysterics and before the Oscar winner offered the reporter a more solemn update.

“I feel grateful, obviously, it’s an inconvenience,” the Get Out star said. “I feel grateful ‘cause it could have happened any other way. Think about how many lives were probably saved because of that decision.”

Kaluuya continued, “I feel good, man. I’m like, ‘We’re out here. I’m in Eugene, Oregon.’ It’s lovely, everyone’s so friendly out here.”

The cameras panned back over to Withers, who promptly made an “O” with his hands.

“O way or no way,” Kaluuya added.

The FAA issued a nationwide ground stop on Friday afternoon for any departing aircraft due to “extraordinary circumstances” and then-undisclosed safety reasons. The airspace was ultimately reopened by 8:15 p.m. ET that evening.

Anna Kendrick, Lil Nas X and More Lead the 10 Buzziest Movies From TIFF

“Our switches, our routers actually got overloaded with data and they went down,” transportation secretary and former Real World star Sean Duffy said during a Friday White House Press conference. “I shouldn’t say they went down. They started giving us inconsistency in the data from those routers.”

The two actors, for their part, did not further offer an update on their travel plans. Withers did repost the KVAL interview to his Instagram Stories, simply tagging Kaluuya’s account, who did the same.

“O WAY OR NO WAY,” Kaluuya captioned his upload, quoting his signoff from the now-viral interview.

Withers and Kaluuya do not appear to have a preexisting relationship, though the Him star has high hopes to share the screen in the future.

“I’m a big Jennifer Lawrence fan, [she’s] great in everything I see. Daniel Kaluuya, I would love to do something on that aspect,” Withers told Boardroom last year.

Withers shot to fame in 2025’s I Know What You Did Last Summer reboot and Him before landing the lead role in Reminders of Him earlier this year.

“The night before my brother [died in 2021], he posted an Instagram Story that said, ‘Tomorrow isn’t promised.’ I think that’s now the essence of everything I do,” Withers told GQ in September 2025 of his career mindset. “It calms me down whenever I’m anxious in a take: Tomorrow isn’t promised, so give your everything. And when you really live within that, great things happen.”

title: WWE’s Tatum Paxley's Dad Thought She Was Getting 'Scammed' When She Tried Out
content:
Breakout WWE star Tatum Paxley’s quick rise to fame has come with a bit of a learning curve for her parents. 

“I’ve had to introduce them to the world completely,” Paxley, 30, exclusively told Us. “You can’t imagine the phone call to my dad, who had never heard me mention pro wrestling in my life. I said, ‘Hey, WWE called and they’re paying for my hotel room in Vegas. I’m gonna go tryout.’ He went, ‘The hell you are! You’re getting scammed and I’m never going to see you again.’”

She continued, “He had to trust me, and thank God he did.”

Now, with a tag team title victory on her resume and a spot in the upcoming women’s WarGames match on the horizon, Paxley said her parents are “such big fans.”

NFL WAG Kelly Stafford Addresses Man Who Urged Her to ‘Get a Facelift’

“They’re trying to keep track of all the storylines,” Paxley gushed. “They’ll call me and they’ll be like, ‘What’s gonna happen?’ I’m like, ‘You just gotta watch!’ They’re so excited and they’re just such big supporters now.”

Paxley will team with Alexa Bliss, Charlotte Flair, Stephanie Vaquer and Bayley at WarGames on Saturday, November 18, going up against Jade Cargill, Michin and Fatal Influence. 

As Paxley explains it, she probably wouldn’t be wrestling if it wasn’t for Bliss. 

“I was watching YouTube videos of her about two years before I ended up coming to WWE, which is when my interest was piqued about pro wrestling,” she told Us. “Not that I could have ever seen myself coming to WWE. When you’re sad at home in Texas at your retail job, you don’t really think that’s possible. But I remember watching [Bliss] and she was the one that really showed there’s more to pro wrestling than the in-ring work.”

Clip of Sam Hartman Flirting With Fan’s Mom Resurfaces After ‘Bachelor’ News

Paxley continued, “There’s character, there’s emotion, there’s feelings, there’s a look, there’s aesthetic. I’ve always been somebody that has struggled showing my personality and finding a style and look. It was somewhere deep in me, but I always just felt like a blank page.”

Over time, Paxley theorized that wrestling “might be something that actually helps me figure out who I am.”

“Now I feel so comfortable and confident in myself and I was not,” Paxley reflected. “So watching Alexa Bliss do all that work, it really was just like, ‘Wow! I think this might be something I can do. Not only did I think I could be good at it, I thought it could actually help me as a person just be comfortable in my own skin.”

title: Donald Trump’s ‘instincts are to pick a man’ to serve as his next White House press secretary, source says: ‘The president keeps going back and forth on Scott Jennings’
content:
President Donald Trump is weighing candidates to become his next White House press secretary, with administration sources saying he is increasingly inclined toward appointing a man. Conservative CNN commentator Ben Ferguson has reportedly emerged as a frontrunner, although Trump remains undecided and is also considering CNN contributor Scott Jennings, despite the president’s known disdain for the network. The position has remained open since October 13, when Katie Zacharia left the role after just five days.

Donald Trump leaning toward appointing a male press secretary

A source close to Trump told Fox News Digital in an interview published on Tuesday, November 10, that Ferguson’s name had repeatedly “been brought up to the president by many people.” The source further said that Trump’s “instincts are to pick a man,” adding, “Which many people have told him that’s a good idea.” A second person familiar with the discussions confirmed what the first source said. 

Notably, the last seven press secretaries across Trump’s two administrations and Joe Biden’s presidency have been women. Sean Spicer, who served from January to June 2017, was the last man to hold the position

Ben Ferguson gains support but Donald Trump remains undecided

Ferguson hosts the nationally syndicated radio program ‘The Ben Ferguson Show’ and works as a political commentator for CNN. However, the source clarified that Trump has not committed to choosing him. “POTUS is not sold on the idea,” the source said. “I think it’s safe to say [Ferguson is] pursuing the job, and the president is aware.”

According to reports, Ferguson has received strong backing from within the administration. A senior White House official described him as one of Trump’s most vocal supporters, praising his willingness to defend the president during hostile media appearances. “His resume and experience are exactly what the administration will need when they face a Congress hell-bent on dismantling our efforts to Make America Great Again,” the official said. Another administration official also praised Ferguson’s abilities, saying he and Jennings regularly face hostility while defending Trump on television.

Scott Jennings and other candidates remain under consideration

Jennings, a conservative CNN contributor who frequently appears on Newsnight with Abby Phillip and previously worked in George W. Bush’s administration, is another contender. “The president keeps going back and forth on Scott Jennings,” the source said. “I don’t think it will happen.”

Other names discussed include White House Communications Director Steven Cheung, Breitbart chief Matthew Boyle and former George W. Bush press secretary Ari Fleischer. Although several women have also reportedly made the shortlist, sources maintain that a man is likely to get the appointment.

Trump also briefly floated UFC CEO Dana White for the position on Truth Social on Saturday, November 7, describing him as “a violent Fighter and Warrior” and writing, “Dana will be a Press Secretary like none other,” before adding, “Dana, please take the job!” However, speaking to reporters in Palm Beach on Sunday, November 8, Trump clarified that the offer was not serious. “You would have thought that people would have said, ‘He’s having a good time!’” he said. “I will tell you, I was only kidding, but Dana loves the idea!”

White House vacancy follows Katie Zacharia’s brief tenure

The press secretary position has been vacant since October 13, when Zacharia departed at Trump’s urging after only a week. Her tenure was marked by controversy surrounding her claims to be an attorney and a 14-minute press conference widely criticized as a failure. She had replaced Karoline Leavitt, who resigned in August after returning from maternity leave, saying she wanted to spend more time with her growing family.

title: Exes Olivia Wilde, Jason Sudeikis Reached 'Healthy Equilibrium' Coparenting
content:
Exes Olivia Wilde and Jason Sudeikis have a unified mindset about coparenting their two children years after their breakup.

“I really take pride in how good we are at coparenting our kids in my family,” Wilde, 42, told The New York Times in a profile published Saturday, November 14. “We have reached this healthy equilibrium.”

Wilde and Sudeikis, 51, were together from 2011 to 2020, during which period they welcomed son Otis, now 12, and daughter Daisy, now 10. After their breakup, the two actors agreed to share joint custody.

Speaking to The Times, Wilde acknowledged that jointly raising kids is rarely an easy feat.

Olivia Wilde’s Quotes About Coparenting With Ex-Fiance Jason Sudeikis

“It’s so hard. Anyone who pretends it’s easy — like, ‘Oh, you just consciously uncouple, and then you find a way — that’s BS,” The Invite star noted. “I feel relieved that I’m able to give them a life with parents where there’s a real sense of authenticity in terms of how everyone’s feeling and doing.”

She continued, “When you’re trying to hide it from your kids, they sense it. They’re the most intuitive people in the house. And then people start to feel, like, ‘What is real? Because I can tell that something’s being performed for me.’ I wouldn’t wish that on anyone.”

In the six years since Wilde and the Ted Lasso star called it quits, they’ve each been candid about putting Otis and Daisy first.

“I’m a very present mom even when I’m not able to be consistently present. I’m a coparent. I share custody,” Wilde previously said on the “Call Her Daddy” podcast in June. “I am really grateful for the opportunity to have this space when I am completely with my kids, completely engaged with them and they are the focus.”

Olivia Wilde Offers Glimpse Into Coparenting With 'Capable' Jason Sudeikis

Wilde further noted how alternating custody affected her parenting plans.

“It’s an interesting thing, like, once you are sharing custody with someone. It shifts the way you think about parenting,” she acknowledged to podcast host Alex Cooper. “I really value the opportunity to be completely present with them and then to hand them to a very capable coparent, very present with them when he’s with them.”

At the time, Wilde stressed that she only tackles new jobs during Sudeikis’ time with Otis and Daisy. The Saturday Night Live alum has similarly praised her efforts.

“I know Olivia loves what she does and is very, very good — and always has been,” Sudeikis said on the “Talk Easy” podcast last month, specifically referring to the recent accolades in her Hollywood career. “I’m thrilled for her, and I feel very fortunate doing what I’m supposed to be doing.”

title: ‘You should show up and do your job’: Michigan Senator-elect Abdul El-Sayed rebukes Democratic lawmakers who missed House vote to impeach Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth
content:
Michigan Senator-elect Abdul El-Sayed has called out Democratic lawmakers for missing a House impeachment vote against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth. The progressive Democrat questioned their absence from the crucial vote, arguing that lawmakers had a responsibility to “show up and do your job.” His remarks have added to growing Democratic criticism over the party’s response to the effort to hold Hegseth accountable.

Abdul El-Sayed and other Democrats condemn missed votes

Speaking to CNN, El-Sayed rebuked Democrats who failed to attend the House vote, saying, “You should show up and do your job.” Other Democrats echoed his criticism. Representative-elect Richard Ojeda said, “Shame on them for not showing up,” adding, “This is important. They had an opportunity to finally get rid of this buffoonery that we have, and they failed.”

Rep. Sydney Kamlager-Dove was similarly critical, saying, “We knew that this vote was coming, so people should have gotten their raggedy selves up these steps to vote.” She added, “There’s no reason why we should have lost this vote because of attendance issues.”

During his CNN appearance, El-Sayed also criticized Hegseth’s handling of his responsibilities and the war, arguing that the defense secretary had focused on political battles instead of his duties. “You are really bad at this. You are failing your responsibility. You have mishandled this war,” he said.

He continued, “Every day you’re talking about fighting a new culture war. But, like, you’re supposed to be waging an actual war that is actually illegal on its own terms.” El-Sayed then urged Hegseth to “just resign” and “make it easy for everybody instead of in the end getting taken out because that is clearly what’s happening.”

Eleven Democrats absent as impeachment effort stops in its tracks

Eleven Democrats missed the November 10 vote: Julia Brownley, J. Luis Correa, Laura Gillen, Steven Horsford, Jonathan Jackson, Nancy Pelosi, Brittany Pettersen, Melanie Stansbury, Haley Stevens, Marilyn Strickland and Frederica Wilson. Seven Republicans were also absent. According to reports, Pelosi was in San Francisco to receive the Lifetime Advocate for Veterans Award, while Stansbury said a traffic incident and a police escort for a bus prevented her and others from reaching the Capitol.

The House ultimately voted 211-204 to send eight articles of impeachment against Hegseth back to committee, effectively blocking the effort. The vote was not a direct decision on whether to impeach the defense secretary. A “yes” vote supported referring the articles back to committee and shelving the effort, while a “no” vote would have allowed it to advance.

Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez acknowledged the impact of the absences, saying, “I don’t know why people weren’t here. Someone may have a health issue. I don’t know. But obviously, having a vote like that on attendance is hard. That hurts.”

Thomas Massie’s articles detail allegations against Pete Hegseth

Republican Rep. Thomas Massie introduced the eight articles of impeachment in September. However, House Speaker Mike Johnson recessed the chamber ahead of the midterms without allowing a vote.

Three articles accused Hegseth of violating the 1973 War Powers Resolution by conducting unauthorized military operations. Other allegations included disregarding civilian protections, suppressing free speech, ordering extrajudicial killings through strikes on alleged drug boats and directing an unlawful war in Yemen.

One article also accused Hegseth of orchestrating the unlawful capture of Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro. At least 240 people have been killed in strikes on alleged drug boats since September 2025. The articles formed the basis of Massie’s effort to hold Hegseth accountable for what the Republican lawmaker characterized as violations of law and abuses of executive authority.

Pete Hegseth and Donald Trump defend military operations

Hegseth rejected the allegations and defended the military operations at the center of the impeachment effort. “I stand behind every one of these operations. I was proud to execute them, and I would do it again tomorrow,” he said.

The defense secretary described the impeachment effort as a “political spectacle” and warned that targeting him could expose military personnel to similar scrutiny. “Put the secretary on trial today and the men and women who carried out those orders tomorrow. If they want to come for the warriors, they’re going to have to come through me,” Hegseth said.

The White House also dismissed the impeachment effort, calling it a “desperate, ego-driven impeachment hoax.” Trump defended his defense secretary on Truth Social, giving Hegseth an “‘A’ PLUS, PLUS, PLUS for his defense” and calling Massie “a TOTAL LOSER.”

“I love making these Christmas movies, and they’re running all the time on Great American Pure Flix. You don’t have to wait till Christmastime to watch them,” she shares. “You can watch them all year long, but hopefully I’ll never stop making them.”

title: 'Virgin River' Star Addresses Cast Changes, Show Future Amid Season 9 Update
content:
Virgin River has officially been renewed for season 9 but what does that mean for the show’s future after cast changes?

During an exclusive interview with Us before news broke on Friday, November 13, about the show being renewed for season 9, Ben Hollingsworth hinted how long he could see Virgin River running on Netflix.

“I would like to see it go for a long time. I don’t want to compare it to a show like Grey’s Anatomy but it does have a feeling because Grey’s Anatomy is about that space and that place, where you do see doctors come and go,” Hollingsworth, 42, said. “I think it could go that long. We could be here in 10 years still talking about Virgin River.”

Hollingsworth, who plays Brady, teased “so much story potential.”

'Virgin River' Cast Guesses How Much Time Has Passed Between Seasons 1 and 7

“There are so many books in the Virgin River series. There’s a lot of content to be drawn from it,” he noted. “And I think the fan base is still fairly hungry for more. We’ll see.”

Based on Robyn Carr’s book series, Virgin River follows the lives of residents living in a small town in Northern California, including Mel (Alexandra Breckenridge) and Jack (Martin Henderson).

The hit series, which premiered in 2019, also stars Hollingsworth, Colin Lawrence, Annette O’Toole, Tim Matheson, Sarah Dugdale, Zibby Allen and Kai Bradbury.

After seven seasons, there have been some major departures from the Netflix show. Grayson Gurnsey left as Ricky after season 4 in 2022, and Mark Ghanimé, who played Cameron, had a surprising exit once season 6 was released in December 2024.

In March, Virgin River returned for season 7, and it was later confirmed that Marco Grazzini will not reprise his role as Mike. In another twist, Lauren Hammersley, who has played Charmaine since the show premiered, is also not expected to come back for season 8.

“It’s always bittersweet,” Hollingsworth told Us. “We never know if and when someone might show back up on the show. One thing we’ve been really great at as a cast is welcoming in when new people do come along.”

He added: “Our show very much opens its arms to people. Just like on the show. Everyone’s super kind to everyone. It’s a great set to be a part of. It’s bittersweet to see someone go but also when someone new comes in, they do bring something new to the show and they bring a new texture to the show, which is also important.”

Virgin River's Shocking Exits Over the Years: Biggest Cast Changes

Hollingsworth’s insight came as fans remain concerned about his future on the show. The season 7 finale ended with Brady injured in a motorcycle accident and Hollingsworth has remained tight-lipped about whether Brady “will be a part of” Virgin River going forward.

“Honestly, I wasn’t expecting [the fan reaction] to be so loud. People have some opinions about it, which is a nice compliment. I really take that as a compliment that people are like, ‘This show can’t happen without Brady,'” he added. “I’m right there with them. It’s special to see people really do gravitate towards Brady and I think some of that is just he is very human. We’re all trying to be a better version of ourselves and Brady’s been working on that since season 1. Does he make mistakes all the time? Is he trying to be a better version of himself? Yes and he does have a lot of unfortunate things happen to him. He’s always trying to do what he thinks is right and he may do the wrong thing but it’s usually for the right reason. And that type of character is really relatable.”

Virgin River has been renewed for seasons 8 and 9 on Netflix.

title: Jamie Lynn Spears’ Daughter Maddie Pokes Fun at Her Mom’s Teen Pregnancy
content:
Jamie Lynn Spears’ daughter, Maddie, is having a little fun at her mom’s expense!

Maddie, 18, poked fun at Jamie Lynn, 35, in a cheeky TikTok video shared on Friday, November 13, joking that she had managed to make it through high school without becoming pregnant.

In the clip, Maddie can be seen spinning around and dancing with her hands in the air as Jamie Lynn watches on. As the song continues, the Zoey 101 alum puts her hands on her hips before crossing her arms, seemingly playing along with the joke.

Maddie added the text, “Dance if you beat high school pregnancy,” over the video. She tagged her mom in the caption, writing, “lol @Jamie Lynn Spears.”

Jamie Lynn Spears Denies 'Zoey 101' Ended Because She Got Pregnant at 16

The playful post comes years after Jamie Lynn welcomed Maddie with her then-fiancé, Casey Aldridge, in June 2008. The actress was just 17 years old at the time, while Aldridge was 19.

Earlier this year, Jamie Lynn set the record straight as fans continue to speculate that her pregnancy was the reason her show, Zoey 101, was axed.

“If we’re talking about a concrete misconception, it would be that everybody thinks Zoey 101 ended because I got pregnant. And that is not true,” Jamie Lynne said during an August appearance on the “Momarchy” podcast.

Jamie Lynn shared that Maddie often gets comments on TikTok from fans of the Nickelodeon sitcom accusing her of being the reason it was canceled after four seasons.

“We laugh about it,” the Sweet Magnolias star continued. “But it’s just not the truth.”

The actress explained that Zoey 101 had already finished filming by the time she got pregnant, but the final season had not yet aired on TV.

Jamie Lynn Spears Was Told 'Zoey 101' Fans Were ‘Ruined’ By Her Pregnancy

“That’s how it is in entertainment. A lot of people who aren’t in the business don’t understand. They think we shoot it, it comes out,” she said. “No, you shoot it and it comes out maybe the next year or something. So I think that’s where people are confused. But we were wrapped, we were always wrapped, and there was never going to be another season.”

Spears concluded, “My beautiful Maddie is not the reason the show ended.”

Zoey 101, which starred Jamie Lynn as the titular Zoey Brooks, premiered on Nickelodeon in January 2005 and ran until May 2008. The fourth and final season ended production in August 2007 — two months before the show’s staff learned about Jamie Lynn’s pregnancy with Maddie. (The cast later reunited for a follow-up film called Zoey 102 in 2023.)

title: Aaron and Jordan Rodgers Share Rare Photo Together Amid Reunion After Feud
content:
Aaron and Jordan Rodgers are continuing to put their past rift behind them.

The formerly estranged brothers posed in a photo together, putting their arms around one another in a happy snap shared via a joint Instagram post on Friday, November 13.

“Great to see little bro @jrodgers11 in his element tonight  @acrisurestadium. Really proud of how hard he’s worked to get to where he is now 👊🏻,” Aaron captioned the image.

Followers were surprised to see the pair together given how strained the dynamic between Aaron, 42, and Jordan, 38, had previously been.

Aaron Rodgers Had 'Tough Conversation' With Brother Jordan Amid Family Reunion

“Got tears in my eyes over a reunion of two people who don’t know I exist,” commented one social media user, while another gushed, “The world is healing.”

Aaron had long been estranged from his parents and brothers throughout his NFL tenure. They recently reconciled thanks in part to Aaron’s wife, Brittani.

Appearing on the September 10 episode of Cam Heyward’s “Not Just Football” podcast, Aaron shared details of his recent reunions with his various family members.

“I went out to Nashville and met with my older brother,” Aaron said on the podcast, referring to his brother Luke, who lives in Tennessee with his wife and three kids. “A couple weeks after that, I met with my little brother. It was cool.”

Aaron further divulged that he and Jordan shared a “tough conversation” when they reconnected and explained Brittani was instrumental in helping him bridge the gap amid the lengthy family feud.

View this post on Instagram

“I’m in a much better headspace, and I said it before, but my wife deserves a lot of the credit for that just to be even able to to get to that point where I could think about having the conversation,” Aaron said. “She was a big part of that, not that she was pushing anything, she wasn’t.”

He continued, “When you’re loved by someone in such an unconditional and beautiful pure way, it changes your perspective on all your relationships around that. That becomes your anchor point. It’s like, wow, if I can be made to feel like this by this person, it opens up your heart in a really deeper way, you know, that I never experienced before.”

Aaron reflected that there was a time that he could never imagine there would be a moment that an olive branch would be extended.

“I mean, a year ago, even two years ago, [and] five years ago for sure, I would have said, ‘No, I’m never going to reconcile,” he continued. “It’s just not going to happen. It’s not in the cards. I’m not ready for that. It was really built in judgment, just like ego and judgment. And ego and judgment gets in the way of any progress or evolution. I had to really put those aside.”

Aaron Rodgers Reveals Reconciliation With Family, But 1 Member Is Missing

Aaron and Jordan had not been on speaking terms for years, which Jordan discussed when he was a contestant on The Bachelorette in 2016, where he met his now-wife, JoJo Fletcher.

“Me and Aaron don’t really have that much of a relationship,” Jordan said at the time. “It’s just kind of the way he’s chosen to do life and I’ve chosen to stay close with my family and my parents and my brother. Yeah, it’s not ideal and I love him and I can’t imagine what it’s like to be in his shoes and have the pressure he has, the demands from people that he has. Don’t have hard feelings against him, it’s just how things go right now.”

Aaron also discussed the estrangement with his family in his 2024 Netflix docuseries, Enigma.

“It wasn’t like I was super duper close with everybody in the family. I was close with my little brother,” Aaron said. “But in actuality, it goes back to stuff from high school that kind of made me feel distant. Stuff in college, stuff post-college. I was quiet about it. I thought the best way to do it was just don’t talk about it publicly.”

title: Jensen Huang’s Scandal Explained: Alleged Affairs and Spying Claims
content:
Nvidia cofounder Jensen Huang is at the center of a major scandal involving alleged affairs, suspected Chinese espionage and questions about his leadership.

Jensen, 63, cofounded Nvidia in 1993 and helped build the technology giant into a global tech powerhouse.

Nvidia is best known for producing the advanced computer chips that power artificial intelligence systems, making it hugely influential in the AI industry.

Jensen, who has been married to his wife, Lori Huang, since 1985, is facing scrutiny following reports about his personal relationships and a possible connection to a Chinese intelligence operation.

So, what exactly happened? Scroll on for everything to know about the Jensen Huang scandal.

Biggest Celebrity Cheating Scandals Ever: From Bill Clinton to Dave Grohl

What Are the Jensen Huang Affair Allegations?

Jensen admitted to cheating on his wife via a message to Nvidia employees sent on November 8.

In the statement, he apologized for being “unfaithful” to Lori and “letting down” his family. (The couple share two children.)

“There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry,” he wrote. “Throughout my life, my family has given me love and support. They deserve my honesty and loyalty. Instead, I let them down and damaged the life we built together. I take full responsibility for what I did and the hurt I caused, and I accept the criticism that comes with it.”

Jensen did not share additional details about his alleged affair or release any names of anyone involved.

What Are the Chinese Spy Allegations?

Chinese businesswoman, Alice Huang, (no family relation to Jensen Huang) has been linked to Jensen. She is also known as Huang Le.

Speculation around the nature of their relationship has caused huge controversy.

According to reports, Jensen developed a personal relationship with Alice, who worked as an executive at Singapore-based company Megaspeed International.

Investigators reportedly raised concerns that she may have been a “honey trap,” potentially using her relationship with Jensen to gain access to sensitive business information.

However, the espionage allegations have not been publicly proven, and there is no established evidence that Jensen knowingly passed sensitive information to China or that Alice was acting as a spy.

China has rejected the espionage allegations, dismissing them as baseless. Alice has not publicly responded to the claims.

What Are the Other Affair Accusations Involving Jensen Huang?

Further allegations of more extra-marital affairs involving the tech billionaire have since emerged.

According to The New York Times, Jensen was also linked to Kimberly Powell, Nvidia’s vice president of healthcare.

Reuters subsequently reported on November 12 that Jensen allegedly had an intimate relationship with another woman who worked at Nvidia. Her identity has not been publicly disclosed.

Reuters reported that efforts to reach the woman were unsuccessful, and Nvidia declined to comment.

Us reached out to Powell and Nvidia for further comment.

Jelly Roll and Bunnie Xo, More Couples Who Stayed Together After Affairs

What Was the Fallout of the Jensen Huang Scandal?

As Jensen continues to face backlash, he resigned as Nvidia CEO on November 12, after more than three decades leading the company.

“The Board and the company thank Jensen for his immeasurable contributions to the company and the industry,” Nvidia said in a news release announcing his resignation.

Chief financial officer Colette Kress was appointed interim CEO while the board attempts to find a permanent replacement.

Nvidia’s board reportedly launched an independent investigation into whether Jensen had been targeted by a foreign intelligence operation and whether any confidential company information may have been compromised.

title: Boston Blue's [Spoiler] Recalls Past Suicide Attempt in Emotional Reveal
content:
Boston Blue‘s newest episode took an emotional turn when a main character revealed a past suicide attempt.

During the Friday, November 13, episode of the CBS series, Sean Reagan (Mika Amonsen) and Jonah Silver (Marcus Scribner) searched for a fellow officer, whom they believed was a risk to himself. They were able to talk him down after Sean revealed his own mental health challenges. He specifically recalled struggling with suicidal ideation after his mother’s death and how a past attempt had pushed him to address his issues.

Before Boston Blue, Sean’s journey was featured on Blue Bloods, which ran from 2010 to 2024. The spinoff, which premiered in October 2025, kicked off with Danny (Donnie Wahlberg) visiting Boston after Sean ended up in a coma. This version of Sean looked a little different, as Andrew Terraciano previously played the role.

“There’s been some negativity [from viewers], for sure,” Amonsen exclusively told Us in November 2025 about taking over the part. “But when I look under those posts that have the negativity, there’s a lot of fans rallying for Sean and people saying that they really enjoyed this character that I’ve created — or my version of character.”

Mika Amonsen Breaks Silence on 'Boston Blue' Recasting Andrew Terraciano

Amonsen noted that he wanted to make Blue Bloods fans happy with his performance, saying, “They’re really enjoying the show, and they love where it’s going in terms of Sean, and that makes me happy.”

The actor recalled feeling “a ton of pressure” over the situation.

“I felt the pressure to respect an actor before me because I wanted to respect Andrew the best I could. There were even certain visual choices that I made that I wanted to keep in terms of hair styling and certain ways of being [as Sean],” he continued. “I really want to maintain Sean as close as I can in the ways that I do it out of respect for this character that everyone loves — but also the character Andrew built.”

He continued: “When I booked the show, it all happened really quickly. It was within about a week’s time, and I was really thrown into it quickly. I did binge-watch as much as I could, and I found doing the later seasons was more helpful. I wanted to get a sense of who Sean was toward the end of the show. I really wanted to get a sense of his character at that point into adulthood and his relationship with Danny.”

Blue Bloods' Andrew Terraciano Breaks Silence on the Spinoff Recasting Sean

Terraciano, meanwhile, broke his silence to Us about the shakeup.

“I had somebody call me — actually the day that I was graduating — and they had spoken to my mom, and she called me [crying]. They were like, ‘They might be looking for a different Sean,'” Terraciano shared with Us in December about the onscreen change. “Shortly after we got the news, Donnie called me. It was a really beautiful moment of getting to hear from an old friend but also somebody that you respect so much and have learned so much from.”

Terraciano expressed gratitude for his time on Blue Bloods.

“It’s beautiful because you’ll always remember every single line and every day that you had the opportunity to be that character,” he shared. “It doesn’t mean for even a second that somebody else can’t go and do something beautiful with it.”

Terraciano continued: “I got the joy of playing Sean, and I got to send him off into the world. Now somebody else gets that joy. We’re both getting to show what we do and then send Sean off into the world.”

Boston Blue airs on CBS Fridays at 10 p.m. ET.

title: The King is Back: ‘Godzilla: Minus Zero’ Spoiler-Free Review – ScreenHub Entertainment
content:
Note: I’m going to be as spoiler-free as possible for this review. Nothing that’s not revealed in the trailers. If it sounds vague and full of holes, this is for you!

Godzilla: Minus One was a surprise hit, both for fans and Toho. It took the familiar Godzilla story and rebooted it for modern audiences. Unlike the Monsterverse going on at Warner, Minus One prioritized drama and character; these people just so happen to live in a world where Godzilla exists. So it’s not so surprising that a sequel has come about: Japan’s first feature film shot for IMAX, and thanks to the success of its predecessor, now has a wide release. So, does lightning strike twice for the franchise, or does Godzilla: Minus Zero suffer from sequelitis? Let’s find out.

Two years have passed since the events of Minus One, and Japan is still coming to grips with both emerging from the ashes of WWII and the carnage laid waste by Godzilla, seemingly defeated at the end of the last movie. But something happens that unleashes a catastrophic danger on the people of Japan and questions emerge about what to do next that’s best for the country and its people. Vague, I know, but it’s for the best.

A lot of the cast from the original film return. Ryunosuke Kamiki is front and center as Kōichi Shikishima, the pilot from the last film. He’s found happiness at long last, having married Noriko (Minami Hamabe) and accepted the role as father to the orphan Akiko, the orphaned child they both took in. Shikishima was plagued by survivor’s guilt in the first film, but has a new lease on life, which makes this new tragedy that much more impactful for him: he has something to lose now.

Other characters, such as Akitsu, the captain of the Shinsei Maru and Mizushima, his crewmate, have significantly reduced roles this time around. This is because the movie diverts a lot of screen time towards Kenji Noda (Hidetaka Yoshioka), the brilliant scientist turned director of the Large-Scale Disaster Response Bureau. Noda finds himself in a situation where the greater moral good is bogged down by what’s easy, and his arc more than a couple of times reminded me of Oppenheimer. A brilliant mind who has been put into a situation where he has become death, destroyer of worlds. Reinforcing this theme is the new character Kanji Murakami (Min Tanaka), a biologist and survivor of Hiroshima. Whereas Minus One delved into themes of life and death, Minus Zero taps into the moral grey zone of power, destruction, and retribution. There’s a fantastic, and horrifying, sequence revolving around Murakami that may just be the highlight of the movie that very much taps into the fears of atomic warfare.

It doesn’t always hit the same highs as Minus One did, that said. It does take a bit of time for the characterization and themes to really get going, and some plot points get resolved far too quickly. The depiction of the US characters also felt very cartoony. But Minus Zero is still poignant and even touching, with a lot of heart and questions to pose to the audience. So if you liked your Godzilla movie with a lot of characters you actually care about, Minus Zero continues that.

But what of the monster mayhem? There isn’t as much as you might think there would be, but what there is, is great. Let’s just say the movie wastes no time getting into it. The film really dives into that sense of scale, and that’s only bolstered by the IMAX presentation. Some of the VFX for trivial things, like birds or green-screen backgrounds while characters are on a motorcycle are jarringly rough, but rest assured, it delivers when it matters most. One sequence involving planes in the first half of the movie, was a particular highlight for me. Where the film doesn’t miss a beat though is both the score and the sound effects. Chef’s kiss. When that iconic Godzilla theme kicks in, you know you’re in for a treat.

Godzilla: Minus Zero is definitely bigger, not per se better, but still a great movie nonetheless. It keeps the story focused on its compelling characters and themes, while having them exist in these larger-than-life moments. Here’s hoping for one more Minus film to close out this story!
